$comment: Card styles of the Ukiyo Tides set (Full Art capsule machine), written by art/machine-specs.mjs from career/machines/full-art.json: edit that file and re-run, not this one.
style: Japanese woodblock print (ukiyo-e): flat areas of indigo, Prussian blue and pale cream, bold black key lines, wood-grain texture in the flat colour, stylised curling waves with claw-like foam, a muted coral accent used sparingly.
rules: These are full-art pictures for playing cards: the client draws a small name plate over the top edge, mana symbols at the top right and power and toughness at the bottom right, so keep the main subject in the middle of the panel and the top 15% and bottom 15% calm and uncluttered (sky, ground, water, background texture), with nothing important in the corners. Each panel shows its own subject as one clear, readable scene, the same style and palette as its neighbours, as if the whole row were a matched, limited-edition art series.
spare: an extra painting in the same style: a great curling wave rising to swallow a falling spark of light, the spark snuffed in its foam

items.subject: a great curling wave rising to swallow a falling spark of light, the spark snuffed in its foam
a scholar in a small boat under a storm sky, three paper charms whirling up out of the sea around them
a lone figure on a rock at dusk looking down into a still tide pool that mirrors the moon
a robed sage standing on the crest of a towering wave, one open palm raised to halt the sea
a single long heron's beak spearing a glowing bubble on the water's surface, ripples spreading

the BACK of a playing card in the same style: a symmetrical ornamental design (it is seen upside down too) with a central emblem drawn from this set's theme, framed by a painted border; no logo, no oval, no five dots, no lettering
